$schema: self-describing architecture map for AI agents
readMeFirst: This file is the machine-readable map of the whole codebase, written for an AI agent starting a new feature. Human-facing version: ARCHITECTURE.html. Deep-dive docs: CLAUDE.md (build+conventions), PLAN_STRONG_AI.md (strong-AI spec), JOURNAL_STRONG_AI.md (strong-AI test log). Rule of thumb: game logic lives in engine-ts/src (TypeScript), gets bundled to static/*.js, and the UIs are vanilla JS in static/. Nothing needs a server.

project.name: Dice Throne Simulator
project.oneLine: A Dice Throne (dice-combat board game) engine + AI, with two browser UIs: a dice-keep 'coach' optimizer and a full 'play vs AI' game. Backed by a TypeScript engine bundled to static JS. No server.
project.language: TypeScript (engine) + vanilla JS (UI) + Python (neural-net training only)
project.runtime: Browser (open static/*.html directly) for UIs; Node for sims/calibration; Python+PyTorch for training
project.gameModel: 50 HP, 2 CP income/turn for all heroes; only starting tokens differ. Dice faces classify per-hero into symbols mapped to A(1-3)/B(4-5)/C(6) (some heroes differ, e.g. bw=1-2/3-5/6, py has 4 symbols 1-3/4/5/6). Turn = Upkeep -> Income -> Main -> Offensive Roll (3 attempts, keep/reroll) -> resolve Attack -> opponent Defense -> Discard.

buildCommands.buildCoach: npx esbuild src/index.ts --bundle --format=iife --global-name=Engine --outfile=../static/engine.js && node inline.mjs && node gen-assets.mjs
buildCommands.npmBuild: npm run build  (builds the COACH engine.js + inline + assets; does NOT rebuild game-engine.js)
buildCommands.test: npx vitest run  (or a single file: npx vitest run tests/sim/mb.rules.test.ts)
buildCommands.CRITICAL: static/game-engine.js and static/engine.js are BUILD ARTIFACTS embedding the TS source AND the hero JSON data. After editing engine-ts/src OR any hero.json, you MUST rebuild the relevant bundle or the UIs run stale code/data. game-engine.js is rebuilt with the esbuild command on src/sim/browser.ts (NOT by npm run build).

entryPoints.purpose: Dice-keep optimizer / 'coach'. Click dice, get top-5 optimal keep strategies + per-ability EV board. Supports ONLY hh/bw/fm (src/index.ts imports only those 3 configs).
Full game: human vs AI, ALL 11 heroes. play.js drives the engine; human decisions via interactive.ts; AI = value-greedy.
Auxiliary views: match report, meta stats, verification, 3D dice demo.
The esbuild entry for game-engine.js: re-exports the sim primitives the UI + calibration + strong-AI workers all call (global `Game`).

subsystems.name: Exact dice-keep DP solver ('the coach brain')
subsystems.purpose: Given current dice + rolls remaining + hero state, compute the EV-optimal set of dice to keep, exactly (no search). Recursive DP over all 2^5 keep subsets x 6^n reroll outcomes, memoized. Used BOTH by the coach UI and by the sim's offensive-roll loop.

keyFiles.role: evalState (recursive EV, Map-memoized), calculateOptimalKeep (full coach result: top-5 + ability distribution + board), optimalKeep (LIGHT: just the best keep, for the sim hot path -- 2x faster, bit-identical), augmentTerminalValue/wildcardVariants (safety-net cards Six-It!/So Wild! etc., coach-only)
CharacterConfig<S> interface: each hero plugs in bestAbilityValue/bestAbilityName/buildAbilityBoard/stateKey. AbilityEntry.
enumerateOutcomes, face->A/B/C classification

publicApi: optimalKeep(cfg, dice, rollsRemaining, state) -> number[]  (sim path, added 2026-07-18)
gotchas: evMemo/distMemo are MODULE-GLOBAL and never auto-cleared (call clearCache() between unrelated contexts). Cache keys are strings built by cfg.stateKey -- the #1 profiler hotspot.
totalDice defaults 5 but is 4 when Naraxus steals a die -- solver stays exact.

subsystems.name: Simulation engine (the monolith)
subsystems.purpose: The authoritative game engine: plays full turns for any hero, resolves every ability, phase, token, and card. Deterministic given (heroes, seed, policies).

keyFiles.role: THE monolith. playTurn(state, activeIdx, rng, policies). All phases (upkeep/income/main/offensive-roll/defense/discard) + ALL 11 heroes' ability resolution (applyMBAbility, applyHHAbility... search 'name.startsWith'). runOffensiveRoll. To add/fix an ability's RESOLUTION, it's here.

GameState, PlayerState (hp/cp/hand/deck/tokens/upgradesInPlay/... + human-pref fields like fmForgePref/mbStrengthPref), Tokens bag, WindowAction, WindowContext, DecisionRequest, AbilityCandidate, HeroId
runMatch(heroA, heroB, seed, policies)->MatchResult, createInitialGameState, MAX_TURNS=200, runBossMatch (vs Naraxus 'nx')
resolveResponseWindow: the pass-pass priority loop (Advanced Rules interaction layer). Decision-agnostic: callers pass enumerate+apply closures. MAX_WINDOW_ACTIONS=100 backstop.
completeOffensiveRoll: the keep/reroll loop that calls core/optimalKeep. oracleStateFor builds the per-hero solver state (incl. defenseTax). This is the bridge sim<->solver.
Policy interface (chooseAbility/decide/chooseCardsToDiscard/chooseAttackModifierCards/... one method per decision type). greedyHighestDamagePolicy (dumb baseline).
resolveMatchedAbilities, fullAbilityBoard -- which abilities a dice set can activate
emptyBag, token helpers, TRANSFERABLE_TOKENS
CP (combat points) economy
mulberry32 (seedable), mulberry32Stateful, rollDice, shuffle -- ALL randomness flows through here (determinism)

gotchas: turn.ts is 4000 lines -- use grep, don't read whole. Ability resolution is a big if/else on name.startsWith('AbilityName').
A dead player must set gameOver+winner or the match spins to MAX_TURNS (a 'timeout', signals a bug -- distinct from a mutual-kill 'draw').
The engine is PUSH: it calls policies[p].hook(...) at each decision. The strong-AI seam (GameNode) inverts this to PULL.

subsystems.name: Hero data, rules & EV configs (per-hero, 11 heroes)
subsystems.purpose: Three layers per hero: (1) verified card DATA, (2) special token MECHANICS, (3) EV VALUES the solver uses to score abilities.

keyFiles.role: SOURCE OF TRUTH for a hero's abilities (dicePattern like 'AABB'/'ABBB', baseDamage, defendable, upgradedBy), cards (upgrades + action cards), tokens, diceAnatomy. VERIFIED against physical board/card scans in characters/<Hero>/. NOTE: transcription errors happen -- 2026-07-21 audit fixed Balestra AABB->ABBB (du) and Pyroblast AAAAD->AAAD (py).
TypeScript types for hero.json
heroTemplateFor(heroId), cardById, buildFullDeck -- loads/parses the JSON

Per-hero token MECHANICS not expressible in JSON, e.g. mb.rules.ts (Strengths Ocean/Mountain/Sky gain + Concussion; chooseStrengthKind respects human pref mbStrengthPref), bw.rules.ts (Time Bomb, Agility, Sabotage), hh.rules.ts (Dreadful, Grim Pursuit).

EV VALUES for the DP solver: constants.ts = damage/token values (empirically CALIBRATED), abilities.ts = bestAbilityValue/board, config.ts = the CharacterConfig plugged into core/evaluator. horseman/dreadful.ts = marginal Dreadful-token value.

gotchas: hero.json boardName (e.g. 'Balestra (ABBB)') is used as an IDENTIFIER in multiple places -- if you change it, grep and change ALL occurrences (hero.json, characters/<hero>/abilities.ts, static/play.js, SPEC.md) or ability matching breaks.
Token EV values in characters/<hero>/constants.ts are CALIBRATED numbers -- see calibration subsystem before changing them.
Upgrade-gated ALT abilities (Fancy Feet, Scorch, ...) live in hero.json altAbilities and are NOT on the base board scans.

subsystems.name: Human-vs-AI interactive bridge
subsystems.purpose: Lets play.js drive the synchronous engine for a HUMAN player: pre-armed choices (set a preference before rolling, engine consumes it), defense windows, coach hints.

keyFiles.role: HumanGame class, AiAttackInfo, DefensePrompt. The engine is synchronous, so human conditional choices are PRE-ARMED (e.g. you.mbStrengthPref, you.fmForgePref, you.smDefenseMode) and the engine's policy hooks read them. play.js sets these flags.
The whole play-vs-AI UI (vanilla JS). renderControls() adds pre-arm buttons per hero (addMbBtns, addSmDefBtns, addFmDefBtns...). Reads game-engine.js (global Game).

gotchas: No async pause mid-resolution: human choices that are conditional (only if you roll X) must be pre-armed as a persistent PlayerState field, then respected inside the engine (usually via a `p.humanControlled ? p.<pref> : <ai-heuristic>` branch in sim/hero/*.rules.ts or turn.ts).
play.js is hand-written (not generated) -- update it manually when hero data changes.

subsystems.name: Deployed AI: value-greedy (the current opponent)
subsystems.purpose: The AI that actually plays in play.html and drives calibration. 1-ply lookahead: for each candidate action, clone+replay it through the real engine, encode the resulting state, score with a trained value network (v4). Pick the highest. Strong on the migrated decisions; delegates the rest.

keyFiles.role: createValueGreedyPolicy(net) -> Policy. Implements every Policy hook by scoreCandidatesByReplay. Contains hand-tuned PRIORS (BW always plays upgrades, freebie cards auto-play, sell-cap for perf).
Neural net: fromJSON/forward (v4 value-only MLP), fromJSON2/forward2 (v5 2-head value+policy). The MATH runtime -- Python trains, this infers (browser + node).
encodeState (v4 feature vector). NOTE: v4 layout RESIZES when a hero is added (why v5 exists).
scoreCandidatesByReplay, cloneForLookahead -- the 1-ply replay-and-score core
enumerate* -- legal candidate actions per decision
The trained v4 net weights (window.AI_WEIGHTS). This is the deployed AI's brain. Loaded by play.js and calibration/strong-AI workers.

gotchas: value-greedy is the STRONGEST agent currently (beats the strong-AI research net ~2:1, see JOURNAL_STRONG_AI.md).
It only NEURAL-scores the migrated decisions (chooseAbility/decide/discard); other hooks use hand-tuned heuristics. Dice-keeping is delegated to the exact DP solver (core/optimalKeep), not the net.

subsystems.name: Strong-AI research (AlphaZero self-play) -- EXPERIMENTAL, does NOT yet beat value-greedy
subsystems.purpose: An AlphaZero-style agent: MCTS over a stable-layout 2-head net, self-play generations with gating. Goal: surpass value-greedy. Status (2026-07-21): reliably ~33% vs value-greedy; self-play does not ratchet. Levers under investigation: bigger search, better priors, warm-start from value-greedy. Full log: JOURNAL_STRONG_AI.md.

keyFiles.role: STABLE feature layout (frozen caps + append-only registries). Adding a hero consumes free slots WITHOUT resizing -> the champion net stays valid (warm-start). FEATURE_COUNT_V5=223.
TRAINABLE_HEROES (11, includes mb), TRAIN_MATCHUPS, EVAL_MATCHUPS. Single source of matchups for training/eval.
THE SEAM: converts the engine's PUSH model to PULL for search (deterministic script-replay). currentActor/pendingDecision/legalActions/apply/sampleChance. Parity-tested vs playTurn.
MCTS/PUCT. evaluate=net value at leaves, priors=net policy head, chance nodes = progressive widening (maxChanceChildren, default raised to 20 for dice).
ACTION_SLOTS=256, actionBucket (FNV-1a hash). Hero-agnostic -> new heroes' actions auto-fit the policy head.
Self-play data gen (DTX2 format): MCTS plays, records featuresV5 + visit distribution + outcome. Matchups derived from TRAINABLE_HEROES.
Gating arbiter: agent A vs agent B (net2 champion/candidate, or 'vg' value-greedy, or 'v4'/'v4warm' MCTS-on-v4-net test agents). Matchups from TRAINABLE_HEROES.
Behavior-cloning: value-greedy plays, record (features, chosen-action one-hot, outcome) -> train the net to imitate value-greedy (warm start).
PyTorch trainer. cmd_train (v1 value net), cmd_train2 (v2 2-head). JSON weight format shared with network.ts (parity-checked).

The AlphaZero generation loop: self-play (champion) -> train2 -> parity check -> gate3 (candidate vs champion) -> promote if Wilson-lower-bound>0.5. State in rl-py/weights2/champion.json (gitignored).

gotchas: Two separate nets: v4 (deployed, features.ts, RESIZES on new hero) vs v5 (research, featuresV5.ts, STABLE). Don't confuse them.
chain2 promotion uses Wilson lower bound > 0.5 (anti-noise) -- 88-game tests have +-10% error, use 400+ games for any 'do we beat X' question.
rl-py/weights2/, exp2/, *.log are gitignored. champion_warm.json = best warm-started net.

subsystems.name: EV calibration (empirical token/card values)
subsystems.purpose: Measure the marginal damage-equivalent value of each token/HP/CP/card by counterfactual paired A/B games (same seed, one mutated starting state), so the solver's EV constants are empirically correct. Feeds characters/<hero>/constants.ts.

keyFiles.role: The 'arms' = each starting-state mutation to test (e.g. th_ek1 = Thor +1 Electrokinesis). CALIB_SET env picks a wave (v5/cards/mb). Matchup = hero vs bw.
Parallel launcher (worker_threads), auto-resumes from results/*.jsonl. --seeds N --workers K (4 is the safe max on this machine).
Plays one game via game-engine.js (value-greedy, or greedy for mb since the net doesn't know mb). Reads static/game-engine.js -- REBUILD it after engine changes.
Turns jsonl into the value table: value(asset) = delta-win(asset) / delta-win(1 HP of same hero).
All-heroes win-rate matrix (meta / who-beats-whom).

gotchas: worker.mjs reads static/game-engine.js -- calibration runs STALE unless you rebuild the sim bundle after engine changes.
CPU/thermal: default to <=4 workers for long runs (see CLAUDE.md / user has burned CPU to 100C stacking parallel batches).

subsystems.name: 3D dice rendering (cosmetic)
subsystems.purpose: Physics-based 3D dice roll animation for the UI.

keyFiles.role: three.js + cannon-es dice. Standalone, no game logic.
source

dataFlows.name: Coach (dice-keep optimizer)
steps: returns top-5 keeps + ability EV board -> rendered

dataFlows.name: Play vs AI
steps: human turn: play.js sets pre-armed prefs, calls Game.playTurn with a human policy (interactive.ts) + AI policy (value-greedy)
AI decisions -> valueGreedyPolicy (v4 net from ai-weights.js)

dataFlows.name: Calibration
steps: workers spawn -> worker.mjs -> Game.runMatch (value-greedy both sides)
node calibration/analyze.mjs -> value table -> hand-apply to characters/<hero>/constants.ts -> rebuild -> confirm via bench

dataFlows.name: Strong-AI training
steps: gate3 candidate vs champion -> promote if significantly better

newHeroAbilityFix_or_dicePatternError: Verify against the physical scan in characters/<Hero>/board/ or cards/
grep the boardName string everywhere and update ALL (characters/<hero>/abilities.ts, static/play.js, characters/<Hero>/SPEC.md, and upgrade card `text` fields)
newHero: Scan board+cards into characters/<Hero>/, write SPEC.md
Add engine-ts/src/sim/hero/<xx>.rules.ts for special token mechanics
Register in sim/data/load.ts and oracle.ts config map
For strong-AI: append 'xx' to featuresV5 HERO_REGISTRY + its tokens to TOKEN_REGISTRY (append-only!) + add to matchups.ts TRAINABLE_HEROES (this is warm-start-safe; FEATURE_COUNT_V5 must stay 223)
Add tests, rebuild bundles, add pre-arm buttons in play.js if it has human choices
Calibrate token EV values (calibration/arms.mjs new arms)
newHumanChoice (stop the AI auto-decidin: Add a pref field to PlayerState in sim/types.ts (e.g. xxPref?)

In the resolving code (sim/hero/<hero>.rules.ts or turn.ts), branch: if the chooser is humanControlled and the pref is set, use it; else the AI heuristic. The AI must NEVER set the pref (keeps its calibrated behavior unchanged).
Add a cycling pre-arm button in play.js renderControls (see addMbBtns/addFmDefBtns as templates)
newStrongAIExperiment: Add/adjust an agent in search/gate3.ts (see v4/v4warm sentinels)
Run a BIG gate (400+ games) via a scratch orchestrator -- small tests are noise

topGotchas: REBUILD after edits: static/*.js are bundles embedding TS + hero JSON. Edit source -> rebuild (game-engine.js via esbuild browser.ts; engine.js via npm run build) or UIs/calibration run stale.
Two engines: engine.js (coach, HH/BW/FM only, src/index.ts) vs game-engine.js (full sim, 11 heroes, src/sim/browser.ts). Two nets: v4 (deployed) vs v5 (research).
Determinism is the contract: all randomness flows through sim/rng.ts. Same (heroes, seed, policies) -> same game. The strong-AI GameNode seam relies on this.
Statistical honesty: 88-game A/B tests carry +-10% error -- do not conclude 'we beat X' from them; use 400+ games (lesson learned the hard way, JOURNAL_STRONG_AI.md).
CPU/thermal: <=4 workers for long runs; user has hit 100C stacking parallel batches. Set High Performance power plan + monitor temps for overnight runs.
Hero JSON = source of truth but transcription errors exist -- verify against characters/<Hero>/ scans (2026-07-21 audit found 2).
